EL BALÓN PARADO VA APARTE, en su propio: SET PIECES GO SEPARATELY, in their own addend, and this was the model's last correction. When everything was a single product, the midfield also multiplied the set pieces threat: a team losing the midfield saw even its danger from corners sink. That doesn't hold (a free kick or a corner doesn't depend on possession the way a built-up move does) and the data confirmed it. Now there are two addends, and since the sum of two Poissons is still Poisson, the counting model doesn't change. What changes is that set pieces have their own dependence on the midfield: {} against {}, three times less. It isn't zero (that was tested, and it's worse: corners come from attacking, and attacking needs the ball); what didn't hold was that they depended on it SO MUCH. On average the split is 72 % open play and 28 % set pieces.
EL ESTIMADOR es la suma de goles observa: THE ESTIMATOR is the sum of observed goals divided by the sum of lambdas for that tactic. It isn't a heuristic: it's exactly the maximum likelihood of a multiplicative factor in a Poisson model. With that value, each group is unbiased by construction, and since the groups cover all matches, the whole model stays unbiased.
EL MEDIO CAMPO MULTIPLICA. Una regresión: THE MIDFIELD MULTIPLIES. A Poisson regression uses a log link, meaning it models log(λ) as a sum; if the duel enters as a logarithm, on the outside it ends up multiplying, and its coefficient is an elasticity: the percentage goals grow when that duel grows by one per cent. That's how the midfield enters, since it's what gives you the ball.

EL PRIMER AVISO es sobre el coeficiente: THE FIRST WARNING is about the set pieces coefficient. It's the largest of the three in the goals equation, and the temptation to read it as “corners decide matches” is immediate. It doesn't hold: that duel shares 62 % of its variance with the attack duels, meaning teams good at set pieces are generally the good teams. Removing it from the model, the midfield and attacks rise to absorb what it measured, which is the unmistakable signature of a collinear variable. It stays because removing it makes prediction much worse, not because its number is a tactics lesson.

It's the only place on that screen that forecasts ONE match, and a match is played with an eleven, not with the average of five. LA COPA SE VALIDÓ APARTE ANTES DE CABLEA: THE CUP WAS VALIDATED SEPARATELY BEFORE WIRING IT IN, because nothing guaranteed that a model fitted on league matches would work there. On the collected cup ties: log-loss 0.2106 against a floor of 0.5499, area under the curve 0.9596 and 88.4 % accuracy on who goes through, calibrated and with no need to correct for home advantage. Against this season's three real cup opponents it called the direction in all three. It's better than in the league for a reason that isn't the model's merit: in the cup the draw crosses different divisions, so many ties are uneven and easy.
LA CORRECCIÓN ES UN FACTOR, no un términ: THE CORRECTION IS A FACTOR, not one more term in the regression. Each tactic multiplies the lambda of whoever plays it. It was chosen this way for three reasons: it doesn't change the shape of the Poisson (a multiple of a Poisson is still a Poisson), its maximum likelihood has a closed form, and it can be switched off by setting the factor to 1 without changing anything else.
THE OPPONENT'S IS WEIGHTED, NOT GUESSED. The natural thing would be to take their most frequent tactic, but that punishes twice when wrong: you don't correct the one they played and you over-correct one they didn't. Instead, the SPLIT of their recent tactics is taken and the factors are averaged weighted by frequency, which is the expected factor when the tactic is uncertain. Measured, that recovers half the bias instead of a third.
LA DESCOMPRESIÓN es el término elevado a: THE DECOMPRESSION is the squared term, and it deserves its own paragraph. A clean product of powers squeezed the lambdas towards the centre: where it promised 0.76 goals, 0.68 were scored, and where it promised 3.30, 3.55 were scored. That filled the grid with low scores (233 matches too many in the zero-and-one-goal block) and from there came 115 extra draws. It wasn't a scale problem, because the regression already had the best possible line and a free slope would have come out as 1 by construction: it was about CURVATURE, and it's fixed with the square of the predictor itself. Nor was it the effect one would test first for too many draws (the dependence between both teams' goals), because that was measured and comes out practically zero, and it also preserves totals: it only moves mass WITHIN the low-score block, never out of it, which was exactly what was needed.
LA SEDE SE CORRIGE, porque un resumen la: THE VENUE IS CORRECTED, because a summary dilutes it. Home advantage isn't added separately: it's already inside the ratings, and a team's midfield at home comes out 17.8 % higher than away. The average mixes home and away matches, so uncorrected, the home side came in underrated and the away side inflated. That's why the summary's midfield is adjusted to the venue of the upcoming match, using each team's real mix: a team that has played almost everything at home is barely touched. Only the midfield, because in the other eight zones the home/away difference is 2 % or less. At a neutral venue, or in a hypothetical match with no venue, nothing is corrected; on the opponent page, only for a league or qualifier match.
LO QUE VE LA PANTALLA ES OTRA COSA, y se: WHAT THE SCREEN SHOWS IS SOMETHING ELSE, and it was measured separately. The figures above predict each match with ITS OWN ratings: they measure how well the engine turns ratings into results. But the upcoming match has no ratings yet, so the screen uses the AVERAGE of each team's previous matches. With the same rolling origin, over 2,773 matches where both teams had history: log-loss 0.6924 and 71.3 % accuracy, against 0.6177 and 73.6 % with the match's own ratings and 0.9787 knowing nothing. That gap is the price of not knowing the lineup.
LOS TRES CARRILES DE ATAQUE, EN CAMBIO,: THE THREE ATTACK LANES, ON THE OTHER HAND, ARE AVERAGED (2026-09-12). Until that date they were multiplied together, which said a blocked lane sinks the whole attack however strong the other two are. Hattrick doesn't play like that: it distributes chances BY lane, and if one is closed you attack through another. Now the three enter as a weighted average (30 % for each wing, 40 % for the middle, which is how attacks are distributed) with each lane raised to a common exponent. That exponent is the underlying question: near zero all three would be needed at once, which is exactly the old form as a limiting case; the higher it is, the more the best lane rules. It comes out at 3.39.

Your left attack doesn't face “the opponent”, it faces their right defence, which covers that lane of the pitch. If you measure what share of each duel you take and know how much each one weighs, you can estimate how many goals each team will score; and from an estimate of goals comes, by arithmetic, the probability of each score and therefore of each result.
